tagline: Along the Smoky foothills to a lake over a drowned town.
intro: From I-75 at Lenoir City, US 321 crosses the Tennessee River and runs through Maryville to Townsend, then narrows to two lanes through Wears Valley before the hotels and outlet malls of Pigeon Forge and Gatlinburg. Past Gatlinburg it follows the northern edge of the national park through Pittman Center and Cosby to Newport, and on through Greeneville and Jonesborough. The state's driving directions send the byway from Maryville to Gatlinburg by way of Sevierville on US 441. The road mapped here keeps to US 321 through Townsend.

At Elizabethton the highway reaches its northernmost point and turns itself around, signed southbound in both directions. The byway follows it on toward the North Carolina line and ends at Watauga Lake.

moments.title: Townsend
moments.text: Chartered in 1921 by people from the Little River Railroad and Lumber Company, Townsend keeps a museum of that logging story at one of the park's three gateways.

moments.title: Jonesborough
moments.text: Tennessee's oldest town, founded in 1779, pitches large tents in its parks on the first full weekend of October for the National Storytelling Festival.

moments.title: Watauga Lake
moments.text: The road winds along the shore of a lake the TVA finished in 1948, and the original town of Butler lies at the bottom of it.
